rawModelResponse.episodeSummary: An 82-year-old female with a history of atrial fibrillation (on digoxin), heart failure, and CKD stage 3 presented with nausea, vomiting, and confusion. An episode of junctional bradycardia (rate 38 bpm) was detected, classified as stable. The ECG showed a regular, narrow QRS rhythm with no P waves. Phase 6 analysis of the controlled event window yielded a median heart rate of 38.04 bpm (range 37.931-143.478 bpm) with low confidence in the heart rate measurement and insufficient confidence in QRS duration measurement. The patient's digoxin level was elevated (3.8 ng/mL, reference 0.8-2.0 ng/mL) and she was taking digoxin 0.25 mg daily. She also had hyperkalemia (5.6 mmol/L, reference 3.5-5.1 mmol/L) and renal impairment (creatinine 2.1 mg/dL).
rawModelResponse.detectedEpisodeContext: Stable junctional bradycardia detected in an elderly female with known atrial fibrillation, heart failure, CKD, and recent symptoms of nausea and vomiting. The rhythm is regular with a ventricular rate of 38 bpm, no P waves, and narrow QRS complexes. The event was captured and is classified as stable based on hemodynamics (SBP 104, MAP 76, SpO2 96).
rawModelResponse.mostLikelyEtiology: Digoxin toxicity leading to increased vagal tone and suppression of the SA and AV nodes, resulting in a junctional escape rhythm.
uncertaintyAndMissingData: Phase 6 heart rate measurement has low confidence.
Phase 6 QRS duration measurement has insufficient confidence.
